summary: Sticky prewarm race causes tenant diversion to degraded variant during pinned-version rollout
description: Issue summary: During a staggered pinned-version rollout for redwood/gptj-13b-v1 in us-east, a small cohort of NovaPay tenants were routed to the degraded quantized variant (gptj-13b-quantized-v1) unexpectedly. Impact: ~0.8% of their traffic received degraded responses for ~18 minutes, causing subtle hallucination regressions in production. Environment: production (us-east), dedicated pool for NovaPay. Observed at 2026-02-18T09:12Z. This appears correlated with prewarm handshake operations and a concurrent coordinator prewarm retry that produced a sticky prewarm session on the orchestrator, preventing the normal pin commit and triggering fallback routing paths.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a staged pinned rollout for redwood/gptj-13b-v1 with canary weight 5%
2) Trigger concurrent prewarm by sending prefetched requests to a small tenant cohort with long streaming sessions
3) Simulate an orchestrator prewarm retry (kill prewarm worker during handshake)
4) Observe routing decision and tenant affinity after orchestrator resync

Expected: tenant remains on pinned variant or cleanly falls back without sticky prewarm state. Observed: tenant affinity persisted to an unexpected degraded variant until explicit token refresh or edge reconnection.

investigation_notes: Preliminary: The orchestrator prewarm retry path attaches the previous sticky_prewarm_id if the original prewarm did not complete cleanly. This sticky id is treated by the edge routing layer as an affinity token and exercised during the routing decision, which can prefer compatible degraded variants when the pinned variant prewarm isn't confirmed.

Reproduction: Local reproduction succeeded by killing prewarm worker mid-handshake; router resolved tenant to quantized variant due to sticky affinity header 'x-prewarm-id' being present and unresolved.

Scope: Affected ~0.8% of NovaPay traffic within the canary window; no other customers observed in initial triage. Root cause tied to concurrent prewarm crash + retry within dedicated pool for NovaPay.
Temporary mitigation: Forced routing override removed sticky prewarm header at edge for NovaPay; revert applied once patch shipped.

Code investigation: orchestrator/controller prewarm retry logic needs to generate fresh session ids and ensure pin_commit flag is re-evaluated on retry. Edge should avoid treating incomplete prewarm ids as authoritative for model selection.
resolution: Root cause: prewarm retry logic in orchestrator reused sticky prewarm ids after worker crash, and edge routing used that id to prefer a compatible quantized variant while pin commit was outstanding. Fix: change prewarm retry to generate new prewarm session ids and mark incomplete prewarm sessions as transient so edge ignores them for routing decisions. Deployed patch in orchestrator (PR 1298) and edge-proxy change (PR 447). Emergency override lifted 2026-02-19 03:12Z. Post-deployment verification: monitored for 48 hours; no recurrence. Follow-ups: add unit test for prewarm-retry behavior, add metric for sticky_prewarm reuse, update prewarm runbook.
postmortem_actions: 1) Merge PR github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1298 to ensure fresh prewarm ids on retry
2) Backport fix to stable branch and deploy to dedicated pools (done 2026-02-19)
3) Edge change github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/447 to ignore incomplete prewarm ids for routing decisions
5) Update confluence runbook to include prewarm-retry checklist and verify pin commit after prewarm completes
